Vaccination is known to protect populations against infectious diseases.
Some of the data in Table 3.1 (on page 4) and Fig. 3.1 (on page 6) support this statement.
Describe the data that support this statement and comment on the data that do not support
this statement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The successful eradication of smallpox involved an intensive global vaccination programme.
It is hoped that the same can be achieved with measles.
Outline two features, apart from cost, of the smallpox eradication programme that may have
made it easier to eradicate than measles.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: State precisely the type of immunity gained by receiving a measles vaccine.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Planning the prevention and control of measles using a vaccination programme means that
financial costs must be considered.
State two examples of these costs.

text: Globally, measles is an important disease that mainly affects children. Many deaths from measles
occur in children under five years of age.
Table 3.1 shows the population of six countries in Africa in 2009 and the number of cases of
measles per 100 000 people for the four years 2009 to 2012.
All six countries are classified as low-income countries.
